736	    def declare_prices(self, raw: Any, key: str | None, tenant: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
737	        """Declare the tenant's price table, replacing it as a whole.
738	
739	        The body is a JSON object whose keys name metered types and whose
740	        values are positive integer-cent prices. A type the table omits keeps
741	        the built-in default price. A non-object body, a missing or unknown
742	        field, or a non-positive, non-integer, boolean, or non-finite price is
743	        a validation error that writes nothing. The route requires a tenant
744	        and an idempotency key; repeating the same declaration with the same
745	        key returns the first result without a second replacement, while the
746	        same key on another operation is the usual 409 conflict.
747	        """
748	        if not tenant:
749	            raise ValidationError("tenant id must be a non-empty string")
750	        if not isinstance(raw, dict) or not raw:
751	            raise ValidationError("prices must be a non-empty object of metered types to positive integer prices")
752	        prices: dict[str, int] = {}
753	        for usage_type, value in raw.items():
754	            if usage_type not in USAGE_TYPES:
755	                raise ValidationError(f"unknown metered type: {usage_type}")
756	            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
757	                raise ValidationError(f"price for {usage_type} must be a positive integer")
758	            if value <= 0:
759	                raise ValidationError(f"price for {usage_type} must be a positive integer")
760	            prices[usage_type] = value
761	        document = self.store.encode(prices)
762	
763	        def apply() -> dict[str, Any]:
764	            self.store.connection.execute(
765	                "INSERT INTO prices(tenant, document, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?) "
766	                "ON CONFLICT(tenant) DO UPDATE SET document = excluded.document, "
767	                "updated_at = excluded.updated_at",
768	                (tenant, document, self.store.now()),
769	            )
770	            return {"prices": dict(sorted(prices.items()))}
771	
772	        with self._operation():
773	            return self._idempotent(key, "declare-prices", apply, tenant)

775	    def delete_prices(self, raw: Any, key: str | None, tenant: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
776	        """Remove the tenant's declared price table as a whole.
777	
778	        The body must be an empty object; deleting a table that was never
779	        declared is the same definite empty result as deleting one that was.
780	        After the delete the tenant holds no table of its own, so later bills
781	        use the built-in defaults; recorded usage and bills already taken are
782	        untouched. The route requires a tenant and an idempotency key:
783	        repeating the same delete with the same key returns the first result
784	        without a second effect, while the same key on another operation is
785	        the usual 409 conflict and leaves every table in place.
786	        """
787	        if not tenant:
788	            raise ValidationError("tenant id must be a non-empty string")
789	        self._empty_body(raw, "delete prices")
790	
791	        def apply() -> dict[str, Any]:
792	            # Removing a table that was never declared deletes no row but is
793	            # still the same definite empty result, never an error.
794	            self.store.connection.execute(
795	                "DELETE FROM prices WHERE tenant = ?",
796	                (tenant,),
797	            )
798	            return {"prices": None}
799	
800	        with self._operation():
801	            return self._idempotent(key, "delete-prices", apply, tenant)

823	    def _effective_prices(self, tenant: str) -> dict[str, int]:
824	        """Prices in effect for the tenant at query time.
825	
826	        Declared prices override the built-in defaults per named metered type;
827	        a type the declaration leaves out keeps its default. Read at query
828	        time on the open transaction, so a later declaration never changes a
829	        bill already taken and never rewrites recorded usage.
830	        """
831	        declared = self._declared_prices(tenant)
832	        if not declared:
833	            return dict(USAGE_UNIT_PRICES)
834	        return {**USAGE_UNIT_PRICES, **declared}

836	    def _usage_counts(
837	        self,
838	        tenant: str,
839	        since: datetime | None = None,
840	        until: datetime | None = None,
841	        types: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
842	    ) -> dict[str, int]:
843	        """Cumulative per-type counts of the tenant's usage records.
844	
845	        With no bounds every recorded record is counted, exactly as the
846	        cumulative baseline. ``since`` and ``until`` bound a closed interval on
847	        each record's own occurrence time (``created_at``): a record equal to
848	        either boundary counts. A window with ``since`` later than ``until``
849	        contains no records, so every type is omitted. ``types`` keeps only
850	        records whose metered type is in the set and combines with the window
851	        as an intersection; when it is ``None`` every type is counted.
852	        """
853	        if since is None and until is None:
854	            rows = self.store.connection.execute(
855	                "SELECT type, COUNT(*) AS count FROM usage_records WHERE tenant = ? GROUP BY type",
856	                (tenant,),
857	            ).fetchall()
858	            counts = {row["type"]: row["count"] for row in rows}
859	        else:
860	            rows = self.store.connection.execute(
861	                "SELECT type, created_at FROM usage_records WHERE tenant = ?",
862	                (tenant,),
863	            ).fetchall()

865	            for row in rows:
866	                if not self._within_window(_parse_stored_time(row["created_at"]), since, until):

875	    def _usage_bucket_counts(
876	        self,
877	        tenant: str,
878	        bucket: str,
879	        since: datetime | None = None,
880	        until: datetime | None = None,
881	        types: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
882	    ) -> list[tuple[datetime, dict[str, int]]]:
883	        """Per-bucket per-type counts of the tenant's usage records.
884	
885	        Records are grouped into fixed UTC buckets (``hour`` or ``day``) after
886	        the same closed time-window and metered-type intersection the
887	        non-bucketed query applies, so a bucket holds only records that both
888	        fall in the window and carry a named type. Buckets are returned in
889	        ascending bucket-start order, each holding its present types in
890	        ascending identifier order. A bucket that ends with no record is
891	        omitted rather than reported empty, and a window with ``since`` later
892	        than ``until`` or a filter that matches nothing yields a definite
893	        empty list.
894	        """
895	        wanted = set(types) if types is not None else None
896	        buckets: dict[datetime, dict[str, int]] = {}
897	        rows = self.store.connection.execute(
898	            "SELECT type, created_at FROM usage_records WHERE tenant = ?",
899	            (tenant,),
900	        ).fetchall()
901	        for row in rows:
902	            if wanted is not None and row["type"] not in wanted:
903	                continue
904	            occurred_at = _parse_stored_time(row["created_at"])
905	            if not self._within_window(occurred_at, since, until):
906	                continue
907	            start = _bucket_start(occurred_at, bucket)
908	            counts = buckets.setdefault(start, {})
909	            counts[row["type"]] = counts.get(row["type"], 0) + 1
910	        ordered = []
911	        for start in sorted(buckets):
912	            ordered.append(
913	                (
914	                    start,
915	                    {
916	                        usage_type: buckets[start][usage_type]
917	                        for usage_type in USAGE_TYPES
918	                        if usage_type in buckets[start]
919	                    },
920	                )
921	            )
922	        return ordered

965	    def bill(
966	        self,
967	        tenant: str,
968	        since: datetime | None = None,
969	        until: datetime | None = None,
970	        types: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
971	        bucket: str | None = None,
972	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
973	        if not tenant:
974	            raise ValidationError("tenant id must be a non-empty string")
975	        if bucket is not None and bucket not in USAGE_BUCKETS:
976	            raise ValidationError("bucket must be hour or day")
977	        with self._operation():
978	            with self.store.transaction():
979	                # Prices are read at query time on this transaction: the bill
980	                # prices with the table in effect now, and never revises a
981	                # previously taken answer when a declaration changes later.
982	                unit_prices = self._effective_prices(tenant)
983	                if bucket is not None:
984	                    # Each bucket lists its present types in ascending
985	                    # identifier order with the price in effect at query time
986	                    # and a subtotal of count times that price, then a
987	                    # per-bucket subtotal; the window total is exactly the sum
988	                    # of the listed per-bucket subtotals. A window or filter
989	                    # that matches nothing yields an empty bucket list totaling 0.
990	                    buckets = []
991	                    total = 0
992	                    for start, counts in self._usage_bucket_counts(
993	                        tenant, bucket, since, until, types
994	                    ):
995	                        items = []
996	                        subtotal = 0
997	                        for usage_type, count in sorted(counts.items()):
998	                            unit_price = unit_prices[usage_type]
999	                            line_total = count * unit_price
1000	                            subtotal += line_total
1001	                            items.append(
1002	                                {
1003	                                    "type": usage_type,
1004	                                    "count": count,
1005	                                    "unit_price": unit_price,
1006	                                    "subtotal": line_total,
1007	                                }
1008	                            )
1009	                        total += subtotal
1010	                        buckets.append(
1011	                            {"bucket_start": _format_bucket_start(start),
1012	                             "items": items,
1013	                             "subtotal": subtotal}
1014	                        )
1015	                    return {"bill": {"buckets": buckets, "total": total}}
1016	                items = []
1017	                total = 0
1018	                # Only types with a record in the window and in the type filter
1019	                # appear, each with the price in effect at query time and a
1020	                # subtotal of count times that price; a filter or window that
1021	                # matches nothing yields an empty bill totaling 0.
1022	                for usage_type, count in sorted(self._usage_counts(tenant, since, until, types).items()):
1023	                    unit_price = unit_prices[usage_type]
1024	                    subtotal = count * unit_price
1025	                    total += subtotal
1026	                    items.append(
1027	                        {
1028	                            "type": usage_type,
1029	                            "count": count,
1030	                            "unit_price": unit_price,
1031	                            "subtotal": subtotal,
1032	                        }
1033	                    )
1034	                return {"bill": {"items": items, "total": total}}

1036	    def usage_records(
1037	        self,
1038	        tenant: str,
1039	        types: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
1040	        since: datetime | None = None,
1041	        until: datetime | None = None,
1042	        cursor: int | None = None,
1043	        limit: int | None = None,
1044	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1045	        """Return the tenant's individual usage records, optionally filtered and paged.
1046	
1047	        The query is read-only: it appends no records, writes no events, and
1048	        changes no metering or billing conclusion. Records are ordered by
1049	        ascending occurrence time, with records sharing one instant ordered by
1050	        ascending sequence. ``types`` keeps only records whose metered type is
1051	        in the set; ``since`` and ``until`` bound a closed interval on each
1052	        record's own occurrence time (a window with ``since`` later than
1053	        ``until`` simply matches nothing); ``cursor`` keeps only records with
1054	        a sequence strictly greater than it; ``limit`` caps the page at that
1055	        many records. Filters combine as an intersection and sequences are
1056	        never renumbered, so consecutive pages neither overlap nor skip. A
1057	        tenant with no matching records gets the definite empty list.
1058	        """
1059	        if not tenant:
1060	            raise ValidationError("tenant id must be a non-empty string")
1061	        wanted = set(types) if types is not None else None
1062	        with self._operation():
1063	            with self.store.transaction():
1064	                rows = self.store.connection.execute(
1065	                    "SELECT sequence, type, created_at FROM usage_records WHERE tenant = ?",
1066	                    (tenant,),
1067	                ).fetchall()
1068	                hits = []
1069	                for row in rows:
1070	                    if wanted is not None and row["type"] not in wanted:
1071	                        continue
1072	                    occurred_at = _parse_stored_time(row["created_at"])
1073	                    if not self._within_window(occurred_at, since, until):
1074	                        continue
1075	                    if cursor is not None and row["sequence"] <= cursor:
1076	                        continue
1077	                    hits.append((occurred_at, row))
1078	                hits.sort(key=lambda hit: (hit[0], hit[1]["sequence"]))
1079	                if limit is not None:
1080	                    hits = hits[:limit]
1081	                return {
1082	                    "records": [
1083	                        {"sequence": row["sequence"], "type": row["type"], "occurred_at": row["created_at"]}
1084	                        for _, row in hits
1085	                    ]
1086	                }

1090	    def metrics(
1091	        self,
1092	        tenant: str,
1093	        since: datetime | None = None,
1094	        until: datetime | None = None,
1095	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1096	        """Aggregate the tenant's persisted business facts into run metrics.
1097	
1098	        The query is read-only: it appends no events, writes no usage records,
1099	        and settles nothing (a due timeout stays unsettled until an operation
1100	        observes it), so the answer reflects exactly what is stored. Every
1101	        dimension is always present — a tenant with no recorded facts gets a
1102	        definite all-zero result rather than an error.
1103	
1104	        ``since`` and ``until`` bound a closed interval on the facts'
1105	        occurrence times: a fact whose time equals either endpoint is counted.
1106	        A window with ``since`` later than ``until`` simply contains no facts,
1107	        so every dimension reports zero.
1108	        """
1109	        if not tenant:
1110	            raise ValidationError("tenant id must be a non-empty string")
1111	        with self._operation():
1112	            with self.store.transaction():
1113	                return self._metrics_counts(tenant, since, until)

1115	    def _metrics_counts(
1116	        self,
1117	        tenant: str,
1118	        since: datetime | None,
1119	        until: datetime | None,
1120	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1121	        """Compute the metrics document; the caller validates the tenant and holds a transaction."""
1122	        # A window with since later than until contains no facts at all, so its
1123	        # result is the same definite zero shape as a tenant with no facts.
1124	        empty_window = since is not None and until is not None and since > until
1125	
1126	        distribution: dict[str, Any] = {
1127	            "running": 0,
1128	            "completed": 0,
1129	            "terminated": {reason: 0 for reason in TERMINATION_REASONS},
1130	        }
1131	        # Each execution contributes exactly one status fact: a running
1132	        # execution's fact is its execution_started event, while a completed or
1133	        # terminated execution's fact is the event that established that
1134	        # status. With no window this counts every execution once, exactly as
1135	        # the unfiltered baseline does. An execution has at most one terminal
1136	        # event, so the join never multiplies rows.
1137	        if not empty_window:
1138	            status_rows = self.store.connection.execute(
1139	                "SELECT e.state, COALESCE(t.occurred_at, s.occurred_at) AS at "
1140	                "FROM executions e "
1141	                "JOIN events s ON s.tenant = e.tenant AND s.execution_id = e.id AND s.type = 'execution_started' "
1142	                "LEFT JOIN events t ON t.tenant = e.tenant AND t.execution_id = e.id "
1143	                "AND t.type IN ('execution_completed', 'execution_terminated') "
1144	                "WHERE e.tenant = ?",
1145	                (tenant,),
1146	            ).fetchall()
1147	            for row in status_rows:
1148	                if not self._within_window(_parse_stored_time(row["at"]), since, until):
1149	                    continue
1150	                state = self.store.decode(row["state"])
1151	                status = state["status"]
1152	                if status == "terminated":
1153	                    reason = state.get("termination_reason")
1154	                    if reason in distribution["terminated"]:
1155	                        distribution["terminated"][reason] += 1
1156	                elif status in ("running", "completed"):
1157	                    distribution[status] += 1
1158	
1159	        # Completion, failure, and retry consumption are counted from
1160	        # the recorded node events: condition evaluations and skips
1161	        # append their own event types and are never counted here, and
1162	        # loop body nodes accumulate one event per iteration. A version
1163	        # migration appends no node events, so facts recorded before
1164	        # and after it accumulate under the same node identifiers.
1165	        completions: dict[str, int] = {}
1166	        failures: dict[str, int] = {}
1167	        retries: dict[str, int] = {}
1168	        buckets = {
1169	            "node_completed": completions,
1170	            "node_failed": failures,
1171	            "node_retried": retries,
1172	        }
1173	        if not empty_window:
1174	            rows = self.store.connection.execute(
1175	                "SELECT type, payload, occurred_at FROM events WHERE tenant = ? "
1176	                "AND type IN ('node_completed', 'node_failed', 'node_retried')",
1177	                (tenant,),
1178	            ).fetchall()
1179	            for row in rows:
1180	                if not self._within_window(_parse_stored_time(row["occurred_at"]), since, until):
1181	                    continue
1182	                node_id = self.store.decode(row["payload"])["node_id"]
1183	                bucket = buckets[row["type"]]
1184	                bucket[node_id] = bucket.get(node_id, 0) + 1
1185	
1186	        # Delivery outcomes are counted per outbound HTTP attempt, so
1187	        # a delivery that fails and then succeeds on a retry records
1188	        # one of each; an attempt succeeded exactly when it received a
1189	        # 2xx status code. A delivery document carries the single
1190	        # occurred_at of the delivery record, shared by every attempt
1191	        # recorded in it.
1192	        succeeded = 0
1193	        failed = 0
1194	        if not empty_window:
1195	            rows = self.store.connection.execute(
1196	                "SELECT document FROM deliveries WHERE tenant = ?",
1197	                (tenant,),
1198	            ).fetchall()
1199	            for row in rows:
1200	                document = self.store.decode(row["document"])
1201	                if since is not None or until is not None:
1202	                    occurred_at = document.get("occurred_at")
1203	                    if not isinstance(occurred_at, str) or not self._within_window(
1204	                        _parse_stored_time(occurred_at), since, until
1205	                    ):
1206	                        continue
1207	                attempts = document.get("attempts")
1208	                if not isinstance(attempts, list):
1209	                    continue
1210	                for attempt in attempts:
1211	                    status_code = attempt.get("status_code") if isinstance(attempt, dict) else None
1212	                    if isinstance(status_code, int) and 200 <= status_code < 300:
1213	                        succeeded += 1
1214	                    else:
1215	                        failed += 1
1216	
1217	        # One trigger row exists per settled schedule period, so a
1218	        # repeated settlement of the same period counts nothing more.
1219	        triggers: dict[str, int] = {}
1220	        if not empty_window:
1221	            rows = self.store.connection.execute(
1222	                "SELECT workflow_id, triggered_at, COUNT(*) AS count FROM schedule_triggers "
1223	                "WHERE tenant = ? GROUP BY workflow_id, triggered_at ORDER BY workflow_id",
1224	                (tenant,),
1225	            ).fetchall()
1226	            for row in rows:
1227	                if not self._within_window(_parse_stored_time(row["triggered_at"]), since, until):
1228	                    continue
1229	                triggers[row["workflow_id"]] = triggers.get(row["workflow_id"], 0) + row["count"]
1230	
1231	        return {
1232	            "status_distribution": distribution,
1233	            "node_completions": dict(sorted(completions.items())),
1234	            "node_failures": dict(sorted(failures.items())),
1235	            "retry_consumption": dict(sorted(retries.items())),
1236	            "delivery_succeeded": succeeded,
1237	            "delivery_failed": failed,
1238	            "schedule_triggers": dict(sorted(triggers.items())),
1239	        }
1240	
1241	    @staticmethod
1242	    def _within_window(occurred_at: datetime, since: datetime | None, until: datetime | None) -> bool:
1243	        """Closed-interval membership: a fact equal to either endpoint counts."""
1244	        if since is not None and occurred_at < since:
1245	            return False
1246	        if until is not None and occurred_at > until:
1247	            return False
1248	        return True

1250	    def metrics_export(
1251	        self,
1252	        tenant: str,
1253	        since: datetime | None = None,
1254	        until: datetime | None = None,
1255	    ) -> str:
1256	        """Render the filtered metrics in the Prometheus text exposition format.
1257	
1258	        Every top-level dimension is one metric family named with the
1259	        ``chronicleflow_`` prefix and the dimension's public key. Families
1260	        appear in the documented top-level key order; samples within a family
1261	        are ordered by ascending label value. Every family carries at least
1262	        one zero-valued sample when it has no facts, values are decimal
1263	        integers, every line ends with a newline, and the whole document ends
1264	        with a single newline.
1265	        """
1266	        counts = self.metrics(tenant, since, until)
1267	        status = counts["status_distribution"]
1268	        terminated = status["terminated"]
1269	        # Samples order by their label values: status first (completed, running,
1270	        # then the terminated samples by ascending reason), which is the
1271	        # ascending tuple-of-label-values order.
1272	        lines: list[str] = [
1273	            'chronicleflow_status_distribution{status="completed"} ' + str(status["completed"]),
1274	            'chronicleflow_status_distribution{status="running"} ' + str(status["running"]),
1275	        ]
1276	        for reason in TERMINATION_REASONS:
1277	            lines.append(
1278	                f'chronicleflow_status_distribution{{status="terminated",reason="{reason}"}} '
1279	                + str(terminated[reason])
1280	            )
1281	        for key in ("node_completions", "node_failures", "retry_consumption"):
1282	            groups = counts[key]
1283	            if groups:
1284	                for label_value, value in groups.items():
1285	                    lines.append(
1286	                        f'chronicleflow_{key}{{node="{_prometheus_label(label_value)}"}} {value}'
1287	                    )
1288	            else:
1289	                # A family with no facts still exposes one zero-valued sample.
1290	                lines.append(f"chronicleflow_{key} 0")
1291	        lines.append("chronicleflow_delivery_succeeded " + str(counts["delivery_succeeded"]))
1292	        lines.append("chronicleflow_delivery_failed " + str(counts["delivery_failed"]))
1293	        triggers = counts["schedule_triggers"]
1294	        if triggers:
1295	            for label_value, value in triggers.items():
1296	                lines.append(
1297	                    f'chronicleflow_schedule_triggers{{workflow="{_prometheus_label(label_value)}"}} {value}'
1298	                )
1299	        else:
1300	            lines.append("chronicleflow_schedule_triggers 0")
1301	        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
